newsitem.title: UK: British World Air offers 2 ATR 72 planes for lease.
newsitem.headline: British World Air offers 2 ATR 72 planes for lease.

text.p: British World Airlines said it has offered for open lease one or both of the two ATR 72 aircraft it owns and currently operates on behalf of Shell.
Spokesman Malcolm Ginsberg told Reuters that Shell had told BWA it in future requires only one of the privately-owned UK carrier's aircraft for on-support flying from Aberdeen.
"Shell has cut back from two to a single aircraft for this role and so we have put the ATR 72s on lease offer to assess marketplace reaction," he said.
"Shell has reviewed its future requirements and believes it needs just one aircraft for the Aberdeen support role," he said.
But he stressed that this did not mean BWA was terminating its flying contract with Shell.
"On the contrary. Even if both ATR 72s were leased, we would offer Shell one of our recently-purchased new (British Aerospace) ATPs," he said.
Ginsberg added that the quick-change passenger-to-cargo configuration ATPs offered 68 seats as opposed to 70 by the similarly convertible ATR 70s.
The all-cargo configuration of each was about 7.5 tonnes, he noted.

"For the two ATR 72s, we would accept either passenger or freight offers and the terms could be either wet-lease (covering hire of plane, crew plus insurance and maintenance) or dry-lease (aircraft only)," Ginsberg stated.
"We are alreday talking to customers about the lease of one or both of our ATR 72s," he said. -Bob Murphy -Reuters Air Cargo Newsroom Tel+44 171 542 7706 Fax +5017 -www.racs.com
